column1: # one line per (expected row, compile) that run_cand_oracle.sh compiles with
# the two trace builds. A line PASSES when both builds compile it without an
# oracle abort and both print a `CANDROW` hit for ROW (its [MECH-REACH]:
# the witness reaches the row it is listed for). Every row identity in
# `cand_rows[]` must have at least one line here (K35: a row nothing reaches
# is a row no plant on it can be caught at).
# Columns (TAB-separated): ROW, FLAGS (`-` for none, else space-separated
# compile options), PATTERN (raw, as passed to --pattern). Lines whose FLAGS
# carry a deny bit pin the row the deny LANDS on: a deny bit the table drops
# is caught there and nowhere else.
# [OPT-REVEND] stage 2 put `a\Kb\z`'s inlined hybrid on rev-end (lane revtri):
# `\b` keeps the bounded view at default, the deny keeps the old witness.
# [REQ-HANDOFF-L1] the re-entered handoff: a byte landmark (dotted4's '.',
# K = 3) and a run landmark (sfx-shaped `ing`), and the deny's landing row.
# [CAND-PATH-READS] the three rows of the cycle 9dec5e6f closed, on one compile:
# FIRST `handoff` reads the path, which selects RECOVER `landing`, which reads
# NEXT `handoff-reentry` under the handoff deny (axtri_report.md §2). Unplanted
# it compiles clean; with RECOVER's deny dropped (S844) the default build
# SIGSEGVs here and the trace build aborts `table-read-cycle`.
# D164 B3: `\s+$` now finishes at prio-const; the DFA ENDSET relocate is the
# state-dependent tie, and the two-seed walk under the deny.
# FIN4's VM ENDSET take cell (stage 2): a tie inside the inlined body (lane revtri).
# D164 B3: a constant mark_prio finishes at prio-const, so the witness is the
# state-dependent hybrid, and the two-seed walk under the deny.
# D164 B3 prio-const: a tagged walk whose mark_prio is a constant (DFA route
# D164 B3: the ENDSET verify needs a tie prio-const cannot decide.
